title: Implement POST /api/admin/upload-enriched and GET /api/admin/pending-status
description:
Implement the two admin endpoints that stage an enriched castle JSON upload to /data/pending/ on the NAS-mounted volume. This is Phase 1 of the approved upload-enriched architecture (planning bead: topcastles-70i). No rebuild, no pipeline execution, no UI.

STRICT SCOPE:
- POST /api/admin/upload-enriched
- GET /api/admin/pending-status
- Route-local JSON body limit (express.json({ limit: '10mb' }))
- Validation contract exactly as designed in planning bead
- Atomic writes to /data/pending/castles_enriched.json and /data/pending/meta.json via json-store.writeJson()
- Production-size payload test using new_app/src/assets/data/castles_enriched.json (not a tiny fixture)

NON-GOALS (do not implement):
- No rebuild trigger endpoint
- No pipeline execution inside the container
- No Angular admin UI
- No background worker or scheduler
- No changes to dist/ or assets/data/ at runtime

VALIDATION CONTRACT (enforce strictly, reject before any write):
1. Content-Type must be application/json (415 if not)
2. Body must be a non-empty JSON array (400)
3. Array length >= 500 (400 with message showing actual count)
4. Each element must have castle_code: string, non-empty (400 with index)
5. No duplicate castle_code values (400 with first duplicate)
6. Each element must have latitude and longitude: present and numeric (400 with index)
7. Array must be sorted descending by score_total — (a.score_total ?? 0) >= (b.score_total ?? 0) for each consecutive pair (400 with index, matching generate_prerender_routes.js assertion)

WRITE TARGETS (both atomic via json-store.writeJson):
- /data/pending/castles_enriched.json — the validated payload
- /data/pending/meta.json — { uploadedAt: ISO string, recordCount: number, uploadedBy: 'admin' }

GET /api/admin/pending-status response:
- 200 with meta.json contents if /data/pending/meta.json exists
- 404 { error: 'no pending upload' } if it does not exist

TESTING REQUIREMENT:
- Integration test must send the actual new_app/src/assets/data/castles_enriched.json as the request body, not a synthetic fixture
- Must verify correct 200 response with recordCount matching the file
- Must verify /data/pending/castles_enriched.json was written correctly
- Must test each validation failure case
- Must test GET /api/admin/pending-status before and after upload

ARCHITECTURE RULES:
- adminAuth middleware is already wired on the router — do not bypass it
- Use json-store.writeJson() for both writes — do not open file handles directly
- The route must not touch new_app/src/assets/data/ or new_app/dist/ in any code path
- Body size limit must be applied at route level, not globally (avoid widening global middleware)
close_reason: Staged-upload endpoint pair tightened and smoke verification extended

title: Plan safe architecture for admin-driven enriched castle content updates
description: Plan the safe architecture for admin-driven content updates using uploaded castle data without violating build-time/runtime separation (ADR-007, ADR-009, ADR-010). This is planning-only — no endpoint implementation. Define how refreshed castle content moves from admin input to live production state.
notes:
APPROVED ARCHITECTURE (Gate 2 approved 2026-04-26)

Option A — Staged upload, explicit developer-machine pipeline + deploy.

Lifecycle:
1. Admin POSTs enriched JSON to /api/admin/upload-enriched (ADMIN_TOKEN auth)
2. Runtime container validates payload and writes atomically to /data/pending/castles_enriched.json + /data/pending/meta.json via json-store.writeJson()
3. Developer machine pulls pending file via scp from NAS
4. Developer machine runs: npm run data:lean, data:api, data:sitemap, data:routes, npm run build, ./deploy.sh
5. New Docker image is live; pending file can be archived/deleted

Forbidden:
- Writing to new_app/src/assets/data/ or new_app/dist/ inside the running container
- Mutating prerendered HTML at runtime
- Running npm run build inside the container
- Auto-deploying from inside the container

Validation contract for upload:
- Must be JSON array, non-empty, length >= 500
- Each element: castle_code (string, non-empty), latitude, longitude present and numeric
- No duplicate castle_code values
- Sorted descending by score_total (strict enforcement, not advisory)
- Express body limit: express.json({ limit: '10mb' }) on the route

json-store.writeJson() is appropriate: atomic tmp+rename, mutex-protected, no streaming needed for this payload size.

Rollback: bad staged upload = do nothing. Bad deployed image = git checkout previous castles_enriched.json + pipeline + deploy.

ADRs preserved: ADR-007, ADR-009, ADR-010, constitution.

Implementation sequence:
Bead 1: topcastles-upload-enriched-endpoint (POST + GET endpoints only)
Bead 2: operator docs (docs/deployment.md section)
Bead 3 (optional): Angular admin UI
Bead 4 (optional): scripts/pull-pending.sh convenience wrapper
close_reason: Planning complete. Architecture approved 2026-04-26. Notes contain full approved architecture summary. Implementation bead: topcastles-spl.

title: Fix: Leaflet map not loading in production (CJS/ESM interop)
description: The map failed in production with TypeError: c.map is not a function. title: Plan PWA and offline browsing architecture
description:
## Why this issue exists

The production runtime is now stable (topcastles-7qj closed). PWA/service worker work is the next planned phase per the product roadmap, but it is architecture-sensitive and classified as Spec Kit work. This bead is planning-only — no implementation.

## What needs to be done

Produce a Spec Kit plan covering:

1. **Service worker strategy**
   - Which routes to precache: SPA shell, api/index.json, api/castles.json
   - Cache strategies per route type: precache vs. cache-first vs. network-first vs. stale-while-revalidate
   - How the SW interacts with the Angular SSR/prerender boundary

2. **Offline UX contract**
   - What the app shows when offline (preloaded list? stale detail pages? graceful fallback shell?)
   - Which user flows must work offline vs. degrade gracefully vs. fail with a clear message
   - Favorites read/write behavior offline

3. **Image caching policy for NAS-served /castle-images/***
   - Images are large, NAS-served, and cache-controlled at max-age=1d by the Node server
   - SW must have a deliberate eviction/quota strategy — do not cache all images by default
   - Stale vs. fresh tradeoffs: thumbnails vs. full-size vs. detail photos

4. **Cache invalidation rules**
   - How the SW knows when to update (SW update lifecycle, skipWaiting policy)
   - How to avoid serving stale castle data after a data pipeline regeneration
   - Version/hash strategy for precached assets

5. **Manifest and install behavior**
   - App manifest fields, icons, display mode, theme color
   - Install prompt strategy (proactive vs. passive)

6. **Runtime/build boundary validation**
   - Validate SW approach against ADR guardrails: no runtime mutation of prerendered artifacts
   - Confirm Angular build output is compatible with chosen SW tooling (Workbox vs @angular/pwa vs custom)

## Key architectural question (must be answered before any implementation)

> What must remain fresh vs. what may safely be stale?

This is the actual PWA problem. Getting this wrong causes silent stale-content bugs in production that are hard to detect and harder to roll back.

## Non-goals

- No service worker implementation in this bead
- No @angular/pwa installation
- No manifest file creation
- No icon generation
- No UI changes

## Acceptance criteria

- Spec Kit planning document produced and approved
- Cache strategy matrix defined per route/asset type
- Offline UX contract written and approved
- Image cache policy decided (quota, eviction, opt-in vs. opt-out)
- Cache invalidation rules agreed
- Implementation approach selected (Workbox / @angular/pwa / custom) with rationale
- ADR guardrail compliance confirmed
- Follow-on implementation bead(s) created and scoped from the plan
